title: Private sessions and premium pricing
audience: Yoga and Pilates instructors who offer one-to-one or small private sessions, including sessions in a client's home
learningOutcomes: Run a private session with the same screening and referral steps as a class, and record them
Set a premium price from the time, skill and costs, without making a health outcome claim
Identify the home-visit safety points that are confirmed and those that remain and those that remain open.
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson: WorkSafe Victoria, Health and safety responsibilities (reviewed 3 April 2025); NSW Government, Fitness and gyms (published 18 October 2024; modified 15 April 2026).

instruction.heading: A private session is still a screened session
instruction.body: A private session often earns a higher rate because the instructor gives more attention and adapts the session to one person. The screening, the consent and the referral steps are the same as in a class, and in a private session they matter more because the instructor is alone with the client. Complete the health questionnaire from “Client screening and health-questionnaire boundaries” before the first session, and repeat it when the client reports a change. Record each modification, referral and stop. The business's private session procedure is held in {{business:procedures.approved_sop}}, and the cancellation rule is in {{business:customers.communication_policy}}.

instruction.heading: Private sessions in a client's home
instruction.body: Some private sessions take place in a client's home. WorkSafe Victoria's health and safety responsibilities page (reviewed 03/04/2025) states that a self-employed person's work must not put others at risk, within what is reasonably practicable, and that employers must do the same for customers and the public. Treat the home as a workplace for set-up and safety, and check the room before the session, as “In-home safety, lone-work and room setup” explains for mobile massage. Check the access instructions in {{business:customers.access_instructions}} before entering, and use the lone-worker check-in method from “Lone-worker safety and check-ins” at arrival and departure.

instruction.heading: Pricing a premium private session
instruction.body: A premium private session should be priced from the time it takes, the skill it needs, the preparation, the travel, the equipment and any compliance cost. A premium price must not be used to justify a claim that the session treats a condition or reduces a medical risk. Describe the session by its length, its focus and its included equipment. Advertising and consumer-law rules for health claims were not researched for this course. The pricing method is held in {{business:pricing.pricing_method}}, and the minimum charge in {{business:pricing.minimum_charge}}. Check the price against the cost of each step before it is published.

procedure: Complete the health questionnaire and the referral check before the first private session
Confirm the access instructions and the location, and check the room for hazards before the session starts
Use the lone-worker check-in at arrival and departure, and record the times
Build the premium price from the time, skill, preparation, travel, equipment and compliance costs
Describe the session by its length, focus and included equipment, with no health outcome claim
Record each private session with its screening, modifications, referrals and stops

workedExamples.situation: A client asks for a private session in her home and describes a recent back injury. She asks the instructor to design a session that will 'fix' her back.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the instructor do before agreeing?
workedExamples.reasoning: The injury is a medical question and the instructor must not diagnose or promise a fix. The instructor should refer the client to a medical practitioner or allied health professional for advice before the first session. The instructor can offer to design a session once the client has advice, and must not describe the session as a fix. The referral and the decision should be recorded.

workedExamples.situation: An instructor wants to charge a premium rate for a one-to-one session. The session takes 60 minutes, and the instructor's preparation takes 30 minutes plus 20 minutes of travel.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How should the price be built?
workedExamples.reasoning: The price should include the 60 minutes of session time, the 30 minutes of preparation, the 20 minutes of travel, the equipment and any compliance cost. The premium rate is justified by the skill and time, and the build should be recorded. The price should not be justified by any claim about a health outcome.

equipmentAndPpe: Mat, props and any equipment checked before the session
Phone with signal and the emergency contact list
Lone-worker check-in method, recorded at arrival and departure

commonErrors.error: Skipping the questionnaire because the client is a repeat private client.
commonErrors.prevention: Repeat the questionnaire at intervals and whenever a change is reported.

commonErrors.error: Promising that a private session will fix a condition.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe the session by its length, focus and equipment. Refer medical questions.

commonErrors.error: Entering a client's home without checking the access instructions.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the access instructions and the room before entering, and record the check-in.

commonErrors.error: Assuming the home visit carries no WHS duty.
commonErrors.prevention: Treat the home as a workplace for set-up and safety, as the confirmed Victorian duties suggest, and check the home point with the regulator.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: WorkSafe Victoria states that a self-employed person's work must not expose others to risk, within what is reasonably practicable, and that employers must do the same for customers and the public. This is confirmed for Victoria.
WorkSafe does not say this directly.
A private session does not grant a licence, a clinical authority or any approval to treat a condition.

qualityStandard: Every private session has a completed questionnaire and a referral check before the first session
The home room is checked and the lone-worker check-in is recorded at each visit
Every premium price is built from its costs and recorded
No private session is described with a health outcome claim
documentationEvidence: Health questionnaire and referral record for each private client
Lone-worker check-in record for each home visit
Price build sheet for each premium session
Session record with modifications, referrals and stops
summary: Private sessions need the same screening and referral steps as classes
Treat the client's home as a workplace for safety.
Price premium sessions from time, skill and costs, never from a health claim
Completing this lesson grants no licence or clinical authority

knowledgeChecks.question: A private client describes a recent back injury and asks the instructor to fix it through a session. What is the correct response?
options: Agree and design a session that will fix the back for the client and the family within a few weeks
Refer the client to a medical practitioner or allied health professional before the first session, and record the referral
Agree, but describe the session as a treatment for the back injury the client described at the first visit

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a premium private session price be built?
options: From the claim that the session treats a condition the client has
From the lowest price in the area the business can find today
From session time, preparation, travel, equipment and compliance costs

knowledgeChecks.question: How does the lesson say a client's home must be treated for a private session?
options: As a private space with no safety duties
As a workplace for set-up and safety
As a club that needs no permit
As a treatment room only after the client signs
